720	At the top, the connection between the head and the body is
721	the throat. The throat is
722	the connector. It joins the thinking part with
723	the animal part, the physical part that man shares
724	with the beast, whose whole purpose is, simply, technically,
725	to allow man to exist. That is, thought, in theory,
726	could exist only in the head without the body. But then
727	man could not bring thought from potential
728	to actual and carry it out. So the execution
729	of thought lies in the instruments of action, the instruments of action from
730	the shoulders
731	down. Thought happens in the head. What happens in the connection?
732	Speech. The throat and the mouth, that is
733	speech. Speech is this
734	connection. Three actions, or three domains of
735	the possibility of
736	human action, and this is an idea that appears in Kabbalah many
737	times. The three fields of action are thought,
738	speech and deed. Deed is the deed of the hands,
739	of the feet, action.
740	Speech is speech,
741	and thought. These are levels, one above
742	the other. In thought everything is found, that is to say,
743	thought is the most fantastic field and the most
744	exclusive, unique to man. Man is able
745	to think, able to understand, able
746	to think. Deed is something man shares with the animals.
747	Many of the deeds we do as human beings
748	we do on an instinctive level, like
749	animals. We are also able to do deliberate
750	deeds, that is, where the deed comes after
751	prior thought. So there is thought and there is deed. What
752	does the throat connect?
753	Speech. Speech, then, is
754	an amazing tool, unique and exclusive to man. Only human
755	beings speak.
756	I mean intelligent speech. True, dolphins
757	supposedly talk, and there is also the language of the birds, but
758	that is chirping,
759	just sounds. It is not intelligent speech. Intelligent speech
760	is exclusive, it is unique to man. And the uniqueness
761	comes from the fact that only man has
762	a soul, a soul in the higher
763	spiritual sense. So the union of body and soul is expressed
764	in speech. This is what gives speech
765	its enormous importance, because, as we said, speech is
766	the garment of
767	thought. If we understand things correctly, then
768	we can understand the commandment
769	in the Torah that one must keep
770	one's word: "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep
771	and do." "He shall not profane his word." If a person says something and does not
772	fulfill it, this is called profaning
773	the word. Let us explain this expression for a moment. It appears, by the way,
774	in the book of Bamidbar, Parashat Matot, in the laws of vows: "If a man
775	vows a vow to HaShem, he shall not profane his word." What does
776	"he shall not profane" the word mean? Not fulfilling it is called
777	profaning it. Let us explain the word "to profane." What is
778	this
779	profanation? In the previous parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê,
780	we learned at the end of the parashah: "If one is found
781	slain, fallen, and it is not known who struck him." What is a "chalal"? Sadly,
782	we know this expression
783	too well from the wars of Israel: "chalalim,"
784	"the fallen." What is a chalal? Why is a person who died or
785	was killed called
786	a chalal? It is also connected to the word
787	"chillul," profanation. Chillul is always a state that is the antithesis.
788	The antithesis of
789	chillul is kiddush, sanctification.
790	Profaning the holy. Shabbat is
791	holy Shabbat. "Those who profane it shall surely be put to death."
792	Profaning Shabbat. Why is it called chillul? The word chillul
793	is connected to the word
794	"chalal," empty space,
795	void. To profane is to take something that has content and remove
796	the content from it.
797	This is called
798	chillul. The people of Israel: when the Holy One, blessed be He, chose us from among all
799	the nations at Mount Sinai, He sent Moshe Rabbeinu
800	and offered us: "You shall be for Me a kingdom of priests and a
801	holy nation." So I always say jokingly that every Jew
802	is really a gentile, only he has to be a
803	holy gentile. "You shall be holy, for I, HaShem, am holy." The people of
804	Israel is a people like all peoples, but it is holy, it has
805	holiness in it. The antithesis of
806	holiness is secularism ("chiloni"). By the way, this expression is a
807	shocking one that we have all grown used to using, but
808	for whoever understands its meaning, people
809	speak and do not understand what they are saying. What does it mean
810	to be a Jew
811	"secular"? "Chiloni" comes from the language of chillul, from the language of
812	uprooting holiness. I am a Jew, but I do not
813	do anything holy. I do not do mitzvot.
814	"Who has sanctified us with His commandments." I do not want to be sanctified
815	by His commandments, and I live my life as if I were not
816	a Jew. Now, if a gentile lives his life as a non-Jew,
817	fine, he is a gentile. But a Jew has
818	the obligation of holiness. When he removes holiness from within himself,
819	he creates
820	a void, a profanation. So a person
821	who was killed, murdered, or from whom his
822	soul departed, a void is created, because the central, supreme,
823	spiritual thing that gives him life, "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of
824	life," He gave breath into them, a soul of life.
825	The soul gives life to the body, so when this soul
826	departs, a void is created. Therefore a person who fell in battle
827	or in general
828	was murdered, not necessarily in battle, also in the Torah, "if one is found
829	slain, fallen in the field, it is not known who," it does not have
830	to be someone who fell in battle. A person from whom
831	his central point has departed, which is
832	the soul. "He shall not profane his word": there is such a thing too. Speech
833	is holy. Whoever understands what we explained about
834	speech, that speech is the action of the holy soul
